facts.statement: The genus Draconichthys was named by Rücklin in 2011.
The only known species in the genus is Draconichthys elegans.
Draconichthys belongs to the class Placodermi.
The genus is classified within the family Selenosteidae.
Fossils of Draconichthys date to the Late Frasnian stage.
The animal lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: Its fossils were found in the Anti-Atlas Mountains of modern-day Morocco.
facts.quote: from the Late Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of the Anti-Atlas Mountains of what is now Morocco

facts.statement: The habitat was a shallow sea dimmed by algae during the Late Devonian.
facts.quote: During the Late Devonian, the region would have been a shallow, algae-dimmed sea

facts.statement: The name Draconichthys elegans translates to "elegant dragon fish".
Its gnathal plates are unusually large and feature long, teeth-like prongs.
facts.quote: Draconichthys elegans differs from all other selenosteids in the structure of its gnathal plates, which are comparatively large, and have long teeth-like prongs

facts.statement: Researchers suggest it was a predator that used its pronged plates to stop prey from escaping.
facts.quote: This feature strongly suggests that it was a predatory animal, and used its pronged gnathal plates to prevent seized prey from squirming out of its mouth

facts.statement: The only known specimen is a skull approximately 112 millimetres long.
facts.quote: D. elegans is currently known from a single skull about 112 millimetres in length

facts.statement: Aside from its unique gnathal plates, its skull anatomy is typical of selenosteids and similar to genera like Enseosteus and Rhinosteus.
facts.quote: The anatomy of its skull, however, is otherwise very typical of selenosteids, being very similar to the genera Enseosteus, Rhinosteus, and Walterosteus
